header.name: Xavier Lacroix
header.role: Computer science student at INSA Lyon
header.bio: I've been a computer science student at INSA Lyon since September 2026. Before that, three years of the BUT Informatique at IUT Lyon 1 (AGED track), including a one-year apprenticeship as a Data Analyst at Lysarc on a national clinical registry. Alongside that I build a lot of personal projects: websites, a homelab, AI agents. What I'm into: data, systems, and turning an idea into something that runs. My aim: Data Engineer and AI Engineer roles.

lysarc.title: The company: Lysarc
body: Lysarc is a non-profit that coordinates academic research on lymphomas. It is based at CHU Lyon Sud and launches a few new clinical trials each year, alongside around fifty ongoing studies.

During my apprenticeship the organisation changed leadership and reorganised: a new roadmap, an innovation hub, and a new department for clinical data engineering. That is what made my missions shift over the year.

I was the only Data Analyst in the organisation. No colleague in the same role, no method to inherit, no referent on my tools. That autonomy forced me to document and justify every choice, which is why documentation and training come with each of my deliverables.

environnement.title: Technical environment
environnement.intro: The registry data fits on a workstation, so it's not a volume problem. The work is organised around two refresh chains, at two speeds.
items: A weekly export from the clinical data-capture tool, which feeds the Power BI dashboards and operational steering.
A SAS processing chain, roughly every six months, which produces the datasets for the official statistical reports.
Windows workstation, SAS and Power BI for analysis, Power BI Cloud for distribution, Visual Studio Code and Git for Python, internal infrastructure for running language models locally.
Part of my documentation work was to keep these two chains clearly separate, so that operational figures are never confused with official ones.
